title: Local invariants of an isomorphism on maximal-ideal completions
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of nonzero commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], each local (having a unique maximal ideal), with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$. Assume $\varphi$ is local, meaning $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Let $i_A:A\to\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}A/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $i_B:B\to\widehat B=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ be the canonical completion maps [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $h:\widehat A\to\widehat B$ be the coordinatewise homomorphism induced by $\varphi$, so $hi_A=i_B\varphi$, and assume $h$ is an isomorphism. Then $h$ carries $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ onto $\mathfrak m_B\widehat B$ and their $n$-th powers onto one another for every $n\ge1$. The actual quotient homomorphism $\varphi_n:A/\mathfrak m_A^n\to B/\mathfrak m_B^n$, $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$, is an isomorphism for every $n\ge1$, and agrees with the quotient of $h$ through the completion projections. In particular the induced residue-field homomorphism $A/\mathfrak m_A\to B/\mathfrak m_B$ is an isomorphism, and $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B=\mathfrak m_B$, where the left side is the ideal generated by the images of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV (lemma-isomorphism-approximation), first proof paragraph: local invariants of the completed stalk isomorphism used for the unramifiedness assertion; algebraic sublemma, not a verbatim statement of the tag.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], the completions are local with maximal ideals $M_A=\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and $M_B=\mathfrak m_B\widehat B$. An isomorphism and its inverse preserve units, hence nonunits. In each completion the nonunits are precisely its maximal ideal, by the cited unit criterion and kernel description. Thus $h(M_A)=M_B$. Expanding ideal products as finite sums of products, and applying $h$ and $h^{-1}$, gives $h(M_A^n)=M_B^n$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tags 05GI (lemma-radical-completion), 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); apply the local-completion statement to A and B.

proof.text: Every ideal of a Noetherian ring is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] to $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$. The coordinate projections $p_{A,n},p_{B,n}$ are surjective ring maps, their composites with $i_A,i_B$ are the original quotient maps, and their kernels are $\mathfrak m_A^n\widehat A=M_A^n$ and $\mathfrak m_B^n\widehat B=M_B^n$. These ideal equalities follow by expanding products: a generator $i_A(a_1\cdots a_n)x$ is a product of $n$ generators of $M_A$, with $x$ absorbed into the last factor; the converse expansion is a finite sum of such generators. The same calculation holds for $B$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), ring case of (2); finite generation is the definition of Noetherianity.

proof.text: Consequently $h$ induces a bijection $\widehat A/M_A^n\to\widehat B/M_B^n$, with inverse induced by $h^{-1}$. The surjective projections with the kernels just computed identify these quotients with $A/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $B/\mathfrak m_B^n$. For $a\in A$, the resulting homomorphism sends $[a]=p_{A,n}(i_A(a))$ to $p_{B,n}(h(i_A(a)))=p_{B,n}(i_B(\varphi(a)))=[\varphi(a)]$. Thus it is the actual $\varphi_n$ and is an isomorphism. By the coordinatewise definition of $h$, also $p_{B,n}h=\varphi_n p_{A,n}$. Taking $n=1$ proves the residue-field assertion.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated): elementary quotient argument using the preceding two steps and the specified coordinatewise map.

proof.text: Put $J=\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, using locality. For any $b\in\mathfrak m_B$, surjectivity of $\varphi_2$ gives $a\in A$ with $b-\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B^2$. Thus $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B$, so $a\in\mathfrak m_A$ by locality. Hence $\mathfrak m_B=J+\mathfrak m_B^2$. The $B$-module $M=\mathfrak m_B$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $J$ is a $B$-submodule whose image in $M/\mathfrak m_BM=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2$ is all of it. Apply the submodule form of [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] over the local ring $B$ to obtain $J=M$, the required equality.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (4), with R=B, M=N′=m_B, N=J, I=m_B; elementary residue comparison uses step 3 for n=2.
